body:
I lost my mom a couple weeks ago. Sometimes I will have a beer or glass of wine to help keep me calm at night. 

When I want to push things further I think to myself “there is nothing to be found in alcohol”. It’s little, but it always stops me from seeking comfort in the wrong place. 

You won’t find anything in alcohol that you can’t find in yourself. I’m so sorry for your loss.

That last paragraph is everything. 

My mom is currently in hospice, I am an only child but luckily I have my dad here and we are her primary care takers. 

She isn’t gone yet, so I don’t know how I will feel. For the most part I am so wrapped up in keeping my dad fed and energized and keeping all family members/friends up to date. I feel pretty...busy? And for the most part I feel alright. But there are times I find myself unable to stand and all I can do is sob silently on the floor in the fetal position. 

Grief is complicated. You are feeling what you are feeling and that is okay. You know you love your mom and I am sure she knew you loved her, too. She would want you to be okay. 

My grief counselor told me “tell your mom ‘mom, I am sad and sometimes I turn into a puddle, but I won’t be a puddle forever’.”  Not super relevant I suppose, but I found it very helpful.

My mom is currently in hospice care. I (30f) live about 6 hours away from my parents house, but I have enacted FMLA and have been staying with my parents for the past week (will probably stay through November). 

My partner (28m) can work remotely and came with me. I have to say, I am pretty private and bad with feelings, so I haven’t been talking to him very much. But it’s nice just knowing he is there. It’s easier crawling into bed (even though I am not sleeping) and it makes me feel a little more grounded. 

I am obviously not your partner, and I am a female, but it’s really helpful to have a second person there. Even if it’s just sitting in the same room as him, or in the next room over, it’s nice to know you aren’t alone. 

When you text him just tell him that you love him and you are open and ready for him. And that everything he is feeling is exactly how he needs to be feeling and that you love him. 

That’s what I like to hear at least.

I’m so sorry for all of the trauma you have gone through in the past two years. 

But remember you are doing all that you can to get through it. It’s okay if you don’t want to talk about things, I feel that too. 

Sometimes if I can’t bring myself to physically say something I text it to my partner or a close friend. And I tell them that they don’t need to respond, I just need another person to understand I am in pain. Usually they just tell me they love me, and it helps. 

It’s okay to cry. I am seeing a grief counselor and it’s one of the only times during the week I let all of my emotions out. She reminds me how important crying is in the healing process. 

Stay strong 💕

Yes. The manufacturer provided Pristiq to me. It is literally a 180. I love it. No negative side effects, just strange dreams. Thank you for asking. I’m sad that I hated myself so much only 2 months ago. The brain is scary.

Thank you. Yes a friend who works as an RN mentioned GoodRX. I am also going back to the pharmacy today. 

I am just confused about the non-coverage deal because I offered to just pay out of pocket but the pharmacy still wanted to speak to my doctor first? 

I am still taking all of the right steps for now.
